evidence.section: 3.1 Thermal Treatment Test and Microstructure Observation
evidence.quote: A temperature load can accelerate the interfacial diffusion reaction behavior of a material and affect IMC thickness. As the temperature increased, the diffusion reaction rate accelerated.
The increase in thermal energy decreased the chemical binding energy and softened the material, and the shear strength decreased significantly in the treatment temperature range of 200-250°C.
In addition, 15-20% oxygen atoms were generated at the failure surface. The high temperature load led to metal oxidation, which decreased the joint strength and caused damage over longer durations.
The IMCs formed faster at higher temperatures.

A reciprocal relationship was observed between material strength and temperature. The mechanical strengths of the as-bonded joint and Au5Sn IMC declined by about 50% as the temperature rose from room temperature to 250°C.
